flag: Other income 25.9% of CFO exceeds 20.0% (FY2023, standalone)
why_chain: Layer 1 (mechanical): other_income_share_of_cfo = other_income/CFO*100. FY2023 CFO (standalone) collapsed to Rs908.24cr from Rs4049.61cr in FY2022 (-77.6% YoY, D-CFO_YOY-FY2023-STAN-066), while other income was Rs235.63cr (F-AR23-003), roughly flat vs FY2022's Rs264.09cr/Rs297.42cr (depending on which restated figure, see RF-MERGE-02). The 25.9% breach is arithmetically a denominator effect, not a numerator (other-income) expansion.

Layer 2 (why CFO fell): FY2023 standalone CFO fell on working-capital absorption in a year revenue was flat (+0.28% YoY, D-REVENUE_FROM_OPERATIONS_YOY-FY2023-STAN-063) but PAT nearly halved (-47.7% YoY, D-PAT_YOY-FY2023-STAN-064) — consistent with commodity-price-driven margin compression (aluminium/alumina cycle down FY2023) rather than a WC-manipulation pattern; inventories and receivables both stayed in a normal low-single-digit-days band (see RF-002/RF-003 why-chains) rather than showing the rising-DSO + rising-inventory + flat-volumes channel-stuffing signature.

Layer 3 (concerning vs benign): Benign explanation supported by: (a) other income itself did not spike — the ratio moves because CFO cratered, and CFO cratering tracks a well-documented commodity down-cycle year for NALCO; (b) no matching rise in receivables/inventory that would indicate CFO understating true cash generation is masked by parking cash outflows elsewhere. Concerning residual: no management quote in the extracted facts explains the specific CFO working-capital swing (extraction did not pull the CFO Note/Schedule reconciliation line items for FY2023), so the WC-leg-level explanation (which leg absorbed cash) is not fully evidenced — this is a disclosure/extraction gap, not evidence of manipulation.

flag: DSO rose 21% YoY (2->2 days) (FY2023, standalone)
why_chain: Layer 1 (mechanical): DSO moved from 1.93 days (FY2022) to 2.34 days (FY2023), a 21.2% relative increase that trips the 20% YoY threshold.

Layer 2 (materiality): both absolute values are in low single-digit days — economically immaterial for a company with Rs14,000-17,000cr revenue. A move from 1.93 to 2.34 days reflects roughly 1.5 additional days' worth of receivables on ~Rs14,255cr revenue (~Rs16cr), not a working-capital or revenue-recognition concern.

Layer 3 (verdict): Percentage-threshold flags on a near-zero base amplify noise into apparent breaches. No corroborating signal (inventory build, customer concentration change, channel-stuffing pattern) accompanies this. Dismissed on materiality grounds.

flag: DSO rose 82% YoY (2->4 days) (FY2024, standalone)
why_chain: Layer 1 (mechanical): DSO moved from 2.34 days (FY2023) to 4.26 days (FY2024), an 82% relative increase — the largest DSO jump in the series.

Layer 2 (materiality and context): still under one working week of receivables outstanding; NALCO's customer base (largely PSU/institutional aluminium and alumina offtake, LME-linked pricing, negligible retail credit risk) structurally supports near-zero DSO. FY2024 revenue fell -7.76% YoY (D-REVENUE_FROM_OPERATIONS_YOY-FY2024-STAN-072) while inventory days also fell (50.83 vs 47.12 in FY2023 -> FY2024 actually rose slightly to 50.83, see D-INVENTORY_DAYS-FY2024-STAN-071) — a rising-DSO-with-flat-or-falling-volumes channel-stuffing pattern would require inventory to be falling while receivables rise (goods shipped out on extended credit); here inventory days also increased modestly, which is more consistent with a demand slowdown than with stuffing.

Layer 3 (verdict): Absolute receivables base remains trivial (single-digit days) relative to revenue scale. Dismissed on materiality; flagged in narrative as a trend to monitor if DSO continues compounding (FY2025 DSO 4.05 days, essentially flat vs FY2024 — trend has stabilized, D-DSO_DAYS-FY2025-STAN-077).

flag: FY26 volume contribution from 5th-stream alumina refinery cut ~40% within one fiscal year (implied ~500KT to 300KT), management-labelled as a revision, then effectively deferred to FY27
why_chain: Q1/Q2 FY26 guidance implied ~5 lakh ton (500KT) FY26 contribution from the new refinery stream.

Q3 (Jan-2026) explicitly revises this to 3 lakh ton (300KT), quote-tagged as a revision by the company itself (GD-Q3-037: 'Previously guided 5 lakh KT for FY26 from new refinery, now more realistic 3 lakh KT').
Q4 (Apr-2026) reframes the entire contribution as an FY27 event (2 lakh ton incremental, GD-Q4-002), consistent with the commissioning start date (June 2026) falling after FY26 (Apr-Mar) close.
management_story: Framed as normal ramp-up conservatism ('optimistic planning') rather than a miss; no explicit acknowledgment that the original 500KT figure implied FY26 delivery.
adjudication_note: Confirmed. Quantified, company-labelled, in-year -40% downward revision of a headline FY26 volume lever, followed by effective one-year deferral to FY27 once the commissioning date moved past FY26 close. Distinguishable from RF-GUI-03/04 (pre-DPR, years-out projects with no near-term delivery commitment): here an original figure implied FY26 delivery and did not arrive. No structural reconciling explanation of the kind that kept guidance.json's own F-GUI-04 (JV cost-sharing rationale) out of red-flag-candidate status is present. Guidance-credibility issue only; no financial-statement/accrual impact.

flag: Alumina export contract mix (spot vs term) target stated inconsistently three times within one fiscal year (80/20 spot-heavy at Q1, 50/50 at Q2 via a quote flagged as an evasive answer, spot-only by Q4)
why_chain: Q1 (Aug-2025): 80% spot / 20% long-term stated as a deliberate strategic shift.

Q2 (Nov-2025): 50% term / 50% spot stated as the target mix; underlying quote reference itself flagged 'refusal_Q2_contract_mix' in the source extraction, indicating an evasive or non-committal management answer.
Q4 (Apr-2026): no long-term contracts being written at all, spot-only, attributed to the low-price environment.
management_story: Each individual quarter's framing is plausible on its own (tracking realized pricing), but no quarter reconciles its stated mix with the prior quarter's stated target.
adjudication_note: Confirmed at low severity. Three genuinely distinct stated positions on the same commercial-mix variable within one fiscal year; the extraction-layer 'refusal_Q2_contract_mix' tag is independent corroboration of an evasive Q2 answer, not merely my inference. Mitigating: the drift direction (toward spot) is at least internally consistent with the stated falling-price rationale, which is why severity is kept low rather than medium. No revenue-recognition or financial-statement impact; guidance-consistency issue only.
